cc:Work.dc:title: Industrial emissions and carbon capture
cc:Work.dc:description: Global sector greenhouse-gas emissions (a), shares of all-industry greenhouse-gas emissions (b), derived emissions per tonne of material (c), and CO2 capture relative to reported sector GHG emissions (d) without circular-economy measures. Each panel contains cement, iron and steel, and aluminium under NDC (ndc_noce; solid lines with open circles) and NDC+LTT (baseline_noce; dashed lines with filled squares). Colours identify sectors; line and marker styles identify climate pathways consistently with the energy figure. Values are extracted directly from results_allCE_261008.csv using exact variable and unit selections, summing the 28 model regions once. Panel a converts reported sector GHG from MtCO2e/yr to GtCO2e/yr. These reported emissions are not reduced again by the separately reported capture values. Panel b divides each sector's global GHG emissions by Emissions|GHG|Industry and multiplies by 100; the three plotted sectors do not exhaust total industry. Panel c divides global sector GHG in MtCO2e/yr by global production in Mt/yr, giving tCO2e/t. It is a ratio of global totals rather than an average of regional intensities. Cement uses cement output excluding clinker; steel and aluminium use primary plus secondary output. A nonpositive denominator yields an undefined ratio. Panel d shows 100 × global Carbon Capture|Industry|sector (MtCO2/yr) / global Emissions|GHG|Industry|sector (MtCO2e/yr), matching sector, climate pathway and model year. The denominator is the reported sector GHG series shown in panel a, retained in its original MtCO2e/yr unit, rather than total industry or the other pathway. Capture is not added to or subtracted from that denominator. This indicator compares captured CO2 with reported GHG emissions; it is not a CO2-only capture efficiency or a fraction of reconstructed pre-capture emissions. It is a ratio of global sums, not an average of regional ratios. Nonfinite quantities or nonpositive sector GHG totals yield gaps; finite ratios above 100% are retained. Source data includes original variables, constituent regions, numerators, denominators and conversion factors for audit. Each panel's vertical scale spans both pathways and all three sectors. Markers show supplied years joined by straight lines, without smoothing or displacement. Curves and markers can overlap where source values coincide or are very close; a filled square within an open circle represents overlapping pathway observations. Very small aluminium capture values lie close to zero on the common capture scale. Draft assumption: missing additive activity = zero.
